prompt: In the short run, a firm should shut down if

options.label: A
options.text: Total revenue is less than total cost

options.label: B
options.text: Average total cost exceeds average variable cost

options.label: C
options.text: Revenue is below variable cost

options.label: D
options.text: Economic profit is less than accounting profit

options.label: E
options.text: Total fixed cost is positive

explanation: In the short run, fixed costs remain whether the firm operates or shuts down. Compare total revenue with variable cost to decide whether production improves its result.

prompt: The price-based version of the short-run shutdown rule compares price with

options.label: A
options.text: Average fixed cost

options.label: B
options.text: Average variable cost

options.label: C
options.text: Average total cost only

options.label: D
options.text: Total fixed cost

options.label: E
options.text: Marginal revenue only

explanation: At the relevant output, price at least equal to AVC covers variable cost. Above that threshold, operating also contributes toward fixed cost.

prompt: If total revenue exceeds total variable cost but is less than total cost, a firm should generally

options.label: A
options.text: Exit the market immediately

options.label: B
options.text: Shut down immediately because profit is negative

options.label: C
options.text: Enter another market in the short run

options.label: D
options.text: Produce zero output because fixed cost is sunk

options.label: E
options.text: Operate temporarily despite economic loss

explanation: Revenue above variable cost leaves money to pay part of fixed cost. Operating therefore reduces the loss compared with shutdown.

prompt: If total revenue is less than total variable cost, a firm minimizes its short-run loss by

options.label: A
options.text: Ignoring variable cost

options.label: B
options.text: Expanding until total revenue equals total cost

options.label: C
options.text: Entering the market

options.label: D
options.text: Shutting down and producing zero output

options.label: E
options.text: Continuing to produce the same output

explanation: Revenue below variable cost makes production add to the unavoidable fixed-cost loss. Shutdown avoids that extra loss.

prompt: When a firm shuts down in the short run, it still must pay

options.label: A
options.text: Only opportunity costs with no explicit costs

options.label: B
options.text: Marginal revenue

options.label: C
options.text: Economic profit

options.label: D
options.text: Fixed costs

options.label: E
options.text: All variable costs

explanation: Short-run fixed obligations must be paid even if output is zero. Shutting down does not eliminate them.

prompt: A firm with price greater than average variable cost but less than average total cost is

options.label: A
options.text: Unable to cover variable cost and should shut down

options.label: B
options.text: Economic loss; operate in the short run

options.label: C
options.text: Earning an economic profit and should enter

options.label: D
options.text: Required to exit immediately

options.label: E
options.text: Breaking even exactly

explanation: Price above AVC covers variable cost and part of fixed cost. Price below ATC means the firm still has an economic loss.

prompt: A firm with price below average variable cost should

options.label: A
options.text: Continue producing because fixed cost exists

options.label: B
options.text: Enter the market

options.label: C
options.text: Shut down in the short run

options.label: D
options.text: Ignore variable cost

options.label: E
options.text: Produce whenever price is below ATC

explanation: Price below AVC means sales do not cover variable cost per unit. Production worsens the loss, so the firm should shut down.

prompt: In the long run, firms tend to enter a market when they anticipate

options.label: A
options.text: Economic losses

options.label: B
options.text: Zero output by every incumbent firm

options.label: C
options.text: Total revenue below variable cost

options.label: D
options.text: Economic profit opportunities

options.label: E
options.text: That fixed costs cannot change

explanation: Expected economic profits offer a return above opportunity costs. They attract new firms when entry is unrestricted.

prompt: In the long run, firms tend to exit a market when they anticipate

options.label: A
options.text: Economic losses

options.label: B
options.text: That all inputs are fixed

options.label: C
options.text: Economic profits

options.label: D
options.text: Higher total product

options.label: E
options.text: Positive accounting revenue

explanation: Expected economic losses mean resources can earn more in other uses. Firms leave when exit is possible.

prompt: The distinction between shutdown and exit is that

options.label: A
options.text: Shutdown is temporary; exit is a long-run decision

options.label: B
options.text: Shutdown requires all inputs to be variable

options.label: C
options.text: Shutdown and exit mean exactly the same thing

options.label: D
options.text: Exit occurs whenever fixed cost is positive

options.label: E
options.text: Shutdown is long run and exit is short run

explanation: Shutdown means temporarily producing zero while fixed obligations remain. Exit means leaving the market in the long run.

prompt: A firm can earn an economic loss and still rationally produce in the short run when

options.label: A
options.text: The loss is larger when it shuts down

options.label: B
options.text: Covers variable cost and some fixed cost

options.label: C
options.text: Price is below AVC

options.label: D
options.text: It can avoid all fixed cost immediately

options.label: E
options.text: Revenue is below variable cost

explanation: TR above TVC provides a contribution toward fixed cost. Producing then loses less than shutting down.

prompt: At the shutdown point, price is equal to

options.label: A
options.text: Total revenue

options.label: B
options.text: Economic profit

options.label: C
options.text: Average variable cost

options.label: D
options.text: Average fixed cost

options.label: E
options.text: Total fixed cost

explanation: At P = AVC, revenue exactly covers variable cost. Below that threshold, shutdown avoids additional operating losses.

prompt: If a firm shuts down, its short-run total revenue is

options.label: A
options.text: Zero

options.label: B
options.text: Necessarily positive

options.label: C
options.text: Equal to total variable cost

options.label: D
options.text: Equal to total cost

options.label: E
options.text: Equal to fixed cost

explanation: A shut-down firm produces and sells no output. Its sales revenue is zero.

prompt: If a firm shuts down in the short run, its variable cost is generally

options.label: A
options.text: Equal to total fixed cost

options.label: B
options.text: Zero

options.label: C
options.text: Necessarily positive

options.label: D
options.text: Greater than total cost

options.label: E
options.text: Equal to economic profit

explanation: In the standard model, variable costs arise from production. At zero output, those costs are zero.

prompt: A firm that continues operating while making an economic loss does so because

options.label: A
options.text: Fixed cost disappears when it produces

options.label: B
options.text: Total cost is irrelevant in every decision

options.label: C
options.text: Operating covers variable cost and reduces the loss

options.label: D
options.text: Entry is required

options.label: E
options.text: Economic profit is always positive when price exceeds AVC

explanation: A positive TR - TVC helps pay unavoidable fixed costs. This makes operating preferable to shutdown.

prompt: Which condition is sufficient for a firm to produce a positive output in the short run?

options.label: A
options.text: Price is below average variable cost

options.label: B
options.text: Economic profit must be positive

options.label: C
options.text: Total revenue is below total variable cost

options.label: D
options.text: Price meets or exceeds AVC

options.label: E
options.text: Average total cost must be zero

explanation: At P = AVC, the firm is indifferent because revenue covers exactly variable cost. At P above AVC, operating contributes toward fixed cost.

prompt: Which condition implies a short-run shutdown?

options.label: A
options.text: TR > TC

options.label: B
options.text: TR > TVC

options.label: C
options.text: P < AVC

options.label: D
options.text: P > AVC

options.label: E
options.text: P > ATC

explanation: Price below AVC fails to cover the production-related cost per unit. The firm should produce zero in the short run.

prompt: Which condition implies that producing rather than shutting down reduces a firm's loss?

options.label: A
options.text: P < AVC

options.label: C
options.text: TR < TVC

options.label: D
options.text: TVC > TR

options.label: E
options.text: TR > TVC

explanation: TR - TVC measures the amount left after variable costs. If positive, it pays part of fixed cost and reduces the loss.

prompt: If price equals AVC exactly, the firm is

options.label: A
options.text: Unable to pay any variable cost

options.label: B
options.text: Required to exit in the long run

options.label: C
options.text: Indifferent between producing and temporary shutdown

options.label: D
options.text: Guaranteed an economic profit

options.label: E
options.text: Guaranteed zero total cost

explanation: When P = AVC, operating covers exactly variable cost. Both operation and shutdown then lose the full fixed cost.

prompt: A short-run fixed cost should affect the shutdown decision by

options.label: A
options.text: Becoming a variable cost

options.label: B
options.text: Raising the shutdown threshold from AVC to ATC

options.label: C
options.text: Forcing immediate exit

options.label: D
options.text: Leaves the P-versus-AVC threshold unchanged

options.label: E
options.text: Forcing the firm to produce

explanation: Fixed cost is unavoidable in either short-run option. Revenue and avoidable variable cost determine whether producing adds or reduces loss.

prompt: If economic profit opportunities persist and there are no barriers to entry, the long-run response is

options.label: A
options.text: Exit of firms

options.label: B
options.text: Entry of firms

options.label: C
options.text: Conversion of variable costs into fixed costs

options.label: D
options.text: Shutdown of all incumbents

options.label: E
options.text: A permanent ban on production

explanation: Unrestricted entry lets firms pursue returns above all opportunity costs. Expected economic profits therefore attract entrants.

prompt: If firms expect continuing economic losses and there are no barriers to exit, the long-run response is

options.label: A
options.text: Exit of firms

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in fixed inputs for every firm

options.label: C
options.text: Continued operation forever regardless of losses

options.label: D
options.text: A requirement that price equal AVC

options.label: E
options.text: Entry of firms

explanation: Expected continuing economic losses make remaining in the market unattractive. Unrestricted firms can exit and use resources elsewhere.

prompt: A temporary economic loss does not automatically imply short-run shutdown because

options.label: A
options.text: All losses are accounting rather than economic

options.label: B
options.text: Fixed costs disappear when output is positive

options.label: C
options.text: AVC is always above ATC

options.label: D
options.text: Entry eliminates the loss immediately

options.label: E
options.text: Variable costs may still be covered

explanation: An economic loss alone does not require shutdown. Production can still reduce the loss if revenue exceeds variable cost.

prompt: The long-run entry decision is primarily based on

options.label: A
options.text: Whether AVC is above AFC

options.label: B
options.text: Expected economic profitability

options.label: C
options.text: The current number of employees alone

options.label: D
options.text: Whether the firm shut down for one day

options.label: E
options.text: Whether current fixed cost is sunk

explanation: Positive expected economic profit makes entry worthwhile because revenue exceeds all opportunity costs. New firms enter if no barrier prevents them.

prompt: The long-run exit decision is primarily based on

options.label: A
options.text: Whether fixed cost was paid last month

options.label: B
options.text: Whether price exceeds AVC for one unit

options.label: C
options.text: The existence of any revenue

options.label: D
options.text: Expected economic losses

options.label: E
options.text: Positive economic profit

explanation: Persistent expected economic losses favor leaving the market. Firms exit when they are able to do so.

prompt: If total revenue equals total variable cost, then operating provides

options.label: B
options.text: Enough revenue to cover all costs

options.label: C
options.text: Less revenue than variable cost

options.label: D
options.text: A positive economic profit

options.label: E
options.text: Revenue covers variable cost but no fixed cost

prompt: When TR is greater than TC, the firm is

options.label: A
options.text: Earning an economic profit

options.label: B
options.text: At the shutdown point

options.label: C
options.text: Required to exit

options.label: D
options.text: Earning an economic loss

options.label: E
options.text: Unable to cover variable cost

prompt: When TR is less than TC but greater than TVC, the firm is

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: At zero economic profit

options.label: C
options.text: Economic loss; operate temporarily

options.label: D
options.text: Unable to cover variable costs

options.label: E
options.text: Required to shut down

prompt: When TR is less than TVC, the firm is

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Earning a positive economic profit

options.label: C
options.text: Required to enter

options.label: D
options.text: Covering all total costs

options.label: E
options.text: Necessarily at minimum ATC

explanation: If TR is below TVC at the best available operating output, producing creates an additional avoidable loss. The firm shuts down.

prompt: If a firm exits a market in the long run, it can

options.label: B
options.text: Retain all fixed inputs by definition

options.label: C
options.text: Avoid only variable cost while fixed cost must remain forever

options.label: D
options.text: Ignore economic losses

options.label: E
options.text: Continue producing the same output

explanation: All inputs become adjustable in the long run. Exit lets the firm stop committing resources to continued production in that market.

prompt: A shutdown decision asks whether a firm should

options.label: D
options.text: Enter a new market in the long run

options.label: E

prompt: An entry or exit decision is a

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Short-run fixed-input decision only

options.label: D

reference: PRD-2.A | PRD-2.A.1 RIGOROUS AUDIT 1 — CED SCOPE & CONTENT All 100 items were checked against PRD-2.A.1 and PRD-2.A.2. Short-run questions use the exact CED shutdown comparisons: total revenue versus total variable cost and price versus average variable cost.
